# Incident Postmortem — billing-worker queue backlog

**Status:** Draft for review
**Severity:** Unknown
**Duration:** ~00:19 (09:01Z → 09:20Z)
**Customer impact:** Not captured in thread.

## Summary
A queue-depth alert fired on billing-worker at 09:01 UTC because consumers stopped processing. Restarting the consumers drained the backlog, and depth returned to normal at 09:20 UTC.

## Timeline
| Time (UTC) | Category | Actor role | Event |
|---|---|---|---|
| 09:01 | observation | on-call engineer | Queue depth alert fired on billing-worker. |
| 09:05 | action | platform engineer | Restarted the stuck consumers. |
| 09:20 | observation | on-call engineer | Queue depth back to normal. |

## Contributing factors
1. Consumers stopped processing for a reason the thread does not record.

## Detection gap
Not captured in thread whether the alert fired promptly after consumers stalled.

## Response — what went well
- The backlog drained within 15 minutes of the restart.

## Response — what went poorly
- The cause of the stall was not investigated before restarting.

## Action items
| Action | Owner role | Due |
|---|---|---|
| Capture consumer thread dumps before the next restart | platform engineering | next incident |

## Open questions
- Why did the consumers stop processing?
- Was any billing work delayed long enough to affect customers?
